newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes higher on exporter deals.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes higher on exporter deals.

text.p: The won ended higher against the dollar on Tuesday on exporter deals and dollar sales stemming from expectations of fund inflows ahead of the planned expansion of the foreign stockholding limit on May 2, brokers said.
The won closed at 891.40, compared with Monday's closing of 893.00. It opened at a low of 892.30 and touched a high of 891.20.
"Some dollar supplies are expected because of the foreign ownership expansion," said Kim Jin-kyu of Citibank.
Brokers said the dollar's fall was limited by the yen's fall against the dollar in global markets.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 892.10 on Wednesday, compared with 893.10 today.
Kim of Citibank forecast trading would range from 892.00 to 894.00 on Wednesday, while Ha Jong-soo of the Korea Exchange Bank put it between 892.00 and 895.00.
